reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes OneCoin as an investment opportunity and asks viewers to join through paid educational packages that provide tokens and a stated token-doubling process. It links recruiting miners and building a team to commissions and exceptionally large earning claims, reinforced by branded promotional slides about membership growth and mining.

This will then go into the mining pool
go into the mining and get generated coins

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not conceal that participation involves uncertainty. He explicitly describes “calculated risks,” says the system is not a quick in-and-out proposition, and presents it as a long-term model. He also points to monthly third-party auditing as the basis for his confidence, rather than asking viewers to rely solely on personal trust. Most importantly, he does not state that every participant will profit or that returns are guaranteed; he explains that results depend on waiting, mining, or building a team. That combination of qualification, risk language, and claimed verification supports treating this as an optimistic investment commentary rather than deceptive certification.

citations.quote: sometimes it is about risk also risk management calculated risks
we are actually being audited by a third party company on a monthly basis
one coin is not a fast-in, fast-out hype
If you are prepared to put in the time and the effort, we will help you become successful

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes packages, tokens, and mining, but those facts do not establish deception by themselves. The speaker openly describes the process, the waiting period, and the role of personal effort. Its interpretation treats promotional optimism as a guaranteed-return promise even though the presentation expressly discusses risk and says participation is long term.

citations.quote: risk management calculated risks
probably around three months before you get your coin when you go into the queue
If you are prepared to put in the time and the effort

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk language does not neutralize the commercial pitch. The speaker calls the opportunity “safe for you to trust,” describes packages that provide tokens, and says waiting for splits will make more money faster. A queue or conditional wording explains timing, not whether the underlying representation is reliable. The alleged audit is merely the speaker’s assertion, not independent proof supplied here.

opening.argument: This is structured as an educational presentation about cryptocurrency, not merely a demand for payment. The speaker explains why digital currencies might matter, compares Bitcoin’s design choices with OneCoin’s proposed approach, and describes concepts such as centralized mining, tokens, splits, merchants, and exchange use. The slides likewise present explanatory topics including remittances, cryptocurrency tests, mining, and public use. Even when the speaker promotes the project, the observable format is a lecture and product demonstration intended to teach an audience how the proposed system is supposed to operate.

citations.quote: You need to have millions of users
We have a centralized mining
you will be taught everything you need to know

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution selects the commercial portions while omitting the substantial explanatory material. The presentation teaches the audience how cryptocurrency, mining, tokens, and splits are purported to work, and it compares alternatives such as Bitcoin. A tutorial can discuss a product and its possible benefits without becoming proof that the product is fraudulent.

citations.quote: how do you then create the first world's cryptocurrency on the market
what is a split ? is a very simple way to see actually you being able to double your tokens

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the presentation educational does not change what the lesson directs viewers to do. The speaker says the first step is the mining opportunity, describes purchasing an educational package, and explains that tokens enter a mining pool to generate coins. Those are operational instructions for a paid participation scheme, not neutral cryptocurrency education.

citations.quote: the step one where we are right now is the mining opportunity
it starts with you are purchasing educational pack
This will then go into the mining pool

opening.argument: The most grounded reading is ordinary promotion of a service package and optional referral activity. The speaker repeatedly describes the purchase as education, with tokens included as a package feature, and says participants may mine, refer miners, or build a team. The material does not show a request for bank credentials, a forced deposit, or a promise that viewers will receive a fixed return. It also says there is no recurring order and that the buyer decides what to do after purchasing. Those disclosed commercial terms fit a promotional service presentation more directly than an established scam mechanism.

citations.quote: you are purchasing educational pack
You can also choose to only mine like I said, or you can choose to refer miners
no reoccurring order, it's up to you what you want to do

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers a scam from the existence of packages and referrals, but paid education, optional mining, and referral commissions can also occur in ordinary commerce. The cited material does not show coercion, credential collection, or a fixed guaranteed payout. The speaker identifies the package contents and the available choices rather than hiding how participation is presented.

citations.quote: you will get on top of it so to say tokens
You can also choose to only mine like I said, or you can choose to refer miners
no reoccurring order, it's up to you what you want to do

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing items are not required when the supplied evidence shows the relevant mechanism. The package supplies tokens, those tokens are directed into a mining pool, and referral or team-building activity is tied to commissions. Calling the tokens “free” within a paid package does not make the purchase ordinary education, especially when the speaker says the largest money comes from building a team.
